notes: Dogfooding the VN-01 live matrix showed 1,627 rows gated as source_crosswalk. Volume was suspicious: the disposition came from the loc_attaches heuristic (ayah appears in entry examples), which is not the same question as 'is the display loc canonical'.
The gate question is directly testable as a typed fact: loc is canonical iff loc appears in the wbw-lookup with a matching surface. The loc_attaches heuristic was a proxy, not the fact.
Playbook section 6 countermeasure: test the canonical question directly (loc in wbw-lookup with matching surface) before packeting any crosswalk row; most 'crosswalk' rows are deployable.

Rows passing the direct canonical test moved back to authorable lanes; genuinely non-canonical rows preserved as crosswalk packets. Exact per-bucket split was not recorded at the time (history gap, stated honestly).
Unlocked rows deployed through the fail-closed Lane-8 protocol (prevalidate, byte-exact concat, canary-wait, control-row 33:63:1 liveness, leak scan). VN-01 reached 100.00% (14,052/14,052).
Regression freeze asserts the completed tranche stays 100% rich with exact glosses and source-clean payloads (smoke-vn01 twin of the VN-00 freeze; see VN-OPERATIONS).

The VN-01 lesson applied forward: VN-02's 905 source_crosswalk rows were ALL loc_attaches with display loc canonical and no exact twin, so they were content authoring, not a hard gate (905 to 245 after the content lane, then 0 at freeze).

Lesson returned to the durable playbook twice: section 6 ANDON row (VN-01 false gate) and section 10 scaled-authoring rule (VN-02: test the canonical question directly before packeting a crosswalk row).
